name: Build Mode
lede: Four missions, about ten minutes each. You move from one-off prompts to workflows, agents, and automations you can run every week, and you learn when to trust what comes back. Jump to any mission in any order.
description: Level 4 of an interactive AI course for marketers: four short missions on repeatable workflows, agents, automations, and checking AI output.

missions.name: From Prompt to Process
missions.hook: A good prompt gets you one good answer. A process gets you the same good answer every Friday. Build one for a small bakery and decide who does each step.
missions.objective: Turn a weekly task into a clear process and decide where a person stays involved.

missions.name: Meet the Agent
missions.hook: An agent is an AI that plans steps and uses tools, while you set the goal and the limits. Watch one work, and decide when to let it keep going.
missions.objective: Follow an AI agent through a task and decide when to approve, edit, or stop it.

missions.name: Wire It Up
missions.hook: An automation is a trigger plus some steps. The trick is not building it, it is building it so a bad day cannot hurt you. Watch the risk meter as you go.
missions.objective: Build a simple automation and see how each choice changes the risk.

missions.name: Trust Test
missions.hook: Output that looks fine is not the same as output that is right. Score five drafts two ways, then write the approval rules you will actually use.
missions.objective: Score AI output two ways and set approval rules you will actually use.

recap: A process is steps plus owners. Tag each one Human, AI, or Both.
An agent plans, acts with tools, checks, and reports. You hold the goal, the limits, and the approvals.
An automation is a trigger plus steps. Filters, repeat checks, and drafts keep a bad day small.
Quick looks catch tone, not facts. Set approval rules by risk: always check, spot-check, or run alone.
next: Next up: Level 5, Boss Level. Set strategy and rules, prove the return, and ship a real workflow.
